answer: An attester must stake 10% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. Because the horizon stake is held until the lotus settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the walnut audit lists each exposure. A farm running 126 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation trivial. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
